items.title: How write and read quorum sizes affect the freshness guarantee
items.description: With N=5 replicas total, drag the write quorum (W) and read quorum (R) sliders. The overlap guarantee (W + R > N) is what proves a read is guaranteed to see the latest acknowledged write — watch how few replicas the read set is guaranteed to share with the write set as you shrink either one below the threshold that keeps them.
items.compute: const n = Math.max(params.totalReplicas, 1); const w = Math.min(params.writeQuorum, n); const r = Math.min(params.readQuorum, n); const guaranteedOverlap = Math.max(0, (w + r) - n); return { guaranteedOverlap };

outputs.label: Replicas guaranteed shared between write and read sets

items.title: How long an AP replica can serve stale data during a partition
items.description: Datacenter B (from this unit's bank Scenario) keeps answering reads locally during a partition instead of refusing (an AP choice). The longer the partition lasts, and the more writes per minute the healthy side is making, the more those writes B doesn't know about pile up before the link is restored and B catches up.

params.name: writesPerMinute
params.label: Writes per minute on the healthy side

outputs.label: Writes the partitioned replica doesn't know about yet
